slides: How to make your English richer... without making it flowery.
So, like we said, language richness isn't its own row in the language table. But it's implied, by fitting academic writing.
And the official guide actually says it clearly. Raters consider precision of word usage, and richness of vocabulary.
Today we'll talk about two tools. Referring words, and raising the register, carefully.
Let's look at a sample paragraph.
Wow. As you can see, there's so much repetition. 'The learning material', and 'teachers'.
Teachers, teachers, teachers, teachers. It's almost impossible to read. And of course, that costs points.
Referring words are words we can use instead, so we don't get this kind of repetition.
They can be synonyms, pronouns like 'they' and 'them', words like 'these' and 'those', possessives like 'their', and phrases like 'with them' or 'unlike them'.
So let's see how I can write this paragraph differently, with referring words.
'They' instead of 'teachers'. 'Have been trained' instead of 'studied', that's a synonym. 'The courses they have taken'. 'Unlike them'. 'The national curriculum', 'teaching it'.
So you see how I used different referring words to make the text easier to read.
Now, some examples of raising the register. Just a few, to give you a direction. So you understand what to do, and try it yourself with every word and sentence you come across.
Instead of 'but', you can write 'however', or 'yet'. They're all correct. 'But' is fine. 'However' is just a bit more formal.
'Enough' becomes 'sufficient'. It says the same thing, but it shows a higher register. And 'kids' is everyday English. In the essay, it's 'children'.
Again, these are just a few small examples. You can take almost any sentence and try to raise it, with synonyms that keep the same meaning.
With practice, and depending on your vocabulary, you'll slowly be able to take sentences and raise the language, and show more richness.
Just never at the cost of clarity. Only use words you really control. There's a short practice routine on the card after this lesson. See you in the next one.
